clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with stage 2 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes, forming a classic metabolic‑syndrome picture that most plausibly explains the elevated blood pressure. Concurrently, reduced renal function indicates stage 3 chronic kidney disease, likely multifactorial with contributions from NSAID‑induced nephropathy and CKD‑related anemia. NSAID use also raises the possibility of iron‑deficiency anemia from occult GI loss, while obesity predisposes to obstructive sleep apnea and mood disorders. Secondary endocrine hypertension is considered but deemed low probability given the strong metabolic risk profile. Unexplained platelet distribution width abnormality remains pending repeat testing.

recommended_workup: Repeat CBC to verify PDW abnormality
Calculate eGFR using serum creatinine and record exact value
Obtain full lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides)
Document smoking status and quantify pack‑years
Perform iron studies (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC) plus B12 and folate levels
Renal ultrasound to assess structural kidney disease
Polysomnography to evaluate for obstructive sleep apnea
Upper endoscopy with H. pylori testing (urea breath test or stool antigen) if GI bleed suspected
Comprehensive endocrine work‑up for secondary hypertension (plasma renin activity, aldosterone, cortisol, thyroid panel)
Gynecologic evaluation including menstrual history and pelvic ultrasound if indicated
